questions.question: A 5-year-old girl has foreign body sensation in her eyes. The next day she develops bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis. Then, she has fever (40 degrees) and sore throat.

parts.text: What is the name of the clinical syndrome? (Adult exam: this was given - You suspect oculopharyngeal syndrome)
What is the most likely pathogen?
Besides respiratory tract infections, name 4 manifestations in an immunocompetent adult.

questions.model_answer:
a) Pharyngoconjunctival fever (a syndrome of follicular conjunctivitis, fever, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis).
b) Adenovirus (classically types 3 and 7).
c) Four manifestations of adenovirus infection in immunocompetent adults besides respiratory tract infection: (1) Epidemic keratoconjunctivitis. (2) Acute hemorrhagic cystitis. (3) Gastroenteritis. (4) Meningoencephalitis (other accepted answers include hepatitis, myocarditis, and nephritis, which are rarer extrapulmonary complications).

parts.text: Name two ways to diagnose Adenovirus.

cohort_answer.text: Molecular/Nucleic acid testing of specimens (CSF, Resp panel, GI panel, conjunctivitis panel, blood); Culture.

questions.question: AM 12. Kid presents with conjunctivitis and then gets severe sore throat. Stem says pharyngoconjunctival fever.

parts.text: b. What are 4 other syndromes? (not pulmonary). (2)

cohort_answer.text: a) Adenovirus (especially types 3, 7, 21). b) Hepatitis; Encephalitis/meningitis; Myocarditis; Gastroenteritis; Hemorrhagic cystitis; Pink eye (conjunctivitis).

questions.question: Pharyngoconjunctival fever suspected.
questions.model_answer: Adenovirus is the virus responsible for pharyngoconjunctival fever (classically serotypes 3 and 7).

cohort_answer.text: NAAT - RTPCR - sensitive and specific. Samples: NP, BAL, conjunctival swab, serum. Viral culture - NP throat, conjunctival swabs. Viral antigen assays. Histopathology: look for classic intranuclear inclusions and IHC. Serology
